title: Total Waviness of Numbers in Range II
summary: Given two integers num1 and num2, calculate the total waviness of all numbers in the inclusive range [num1, num2].
statement: Given two integers num1 and num2, calculate the total waviness of all numbers in the inclusive range [num1, num2]. Waviness is the count of peaks and valleys in each number, where a peak is a digit greater than both neighbors and a valley is a digit less than both neighbors. The first and last digits cannot be peaks or valleys, and numbers with fewer than three digits have a waviness of zero.
constraints: A middle digit contributes when it is strictly above both neighbors or strictly below both.
Return total waviness across the inclusive range.
hints: Compute a prefix total F(x), then answer F(num2)-F(num1-1).
A digit-DP state keeps the last two significant digits, whether the number has started, and tightness.
When appending a digit, the previous digit becomes internal and contributes if it is a strict peak or valley.
The DP enumerates every integer once and accumulates both suffix counts and their added waviness.
editorial: The DP enumerates every integer once and accumulates both suffix counts and their added waviness.

tests.explanation: Only 120, 121, and 130 contribute one each, totaling three.
The internal eight and four are a peak and valley, giving two.
